newsitem.title: USA: Tampa Sports Authority, Fla., A2 by Moody's.
newsitem.headline: Tampa Sports Authority, Fla., A2 by Moody's.

text.p: Underlying Issue Local Option Sales Tax Revenue Bonds
(Stadium Project), Series 1997
Rating A2 A2
Sale Amount $150,745,000.00
Expected Sale Date 06/25/97
Rating Description Local Option Sales Tax

NEW YORK, June 20, 1997 -- Moody's has assigned an A2 underlying rating to the Local Option Sales Tax Revenue Bonds (Stadium Project) of the Tampa Sports Authority. MBIA is expected to insure these bonds. Subject to Moody's review and approval of the insurance policy and other relevant documentation, the bonds are expected to carry the insurer's financial strength rating of Aaa. The A2 underlying rating will continue to be maintained. The A2 underlying rating is based on the satisfactory coverage of debt service from a fixed amount of pledged revenues derived from a satisfactory level of sales tax receipts and the fact that this separate capital source has been voter-approved to finance stadium construction.
SATISFACTORY COVERAGE OF DEBT SERVICE FROM PLEDGED SALES TAX REVENUES

Hillsborough County voters have approved a local option half-cent sales tax for the thirty-year life of the bonds. The first 25% portion of this new sales tax goes directly to the school board. The remainder, up to the amount specified in an interlocal agreement with the county and cities, goes first to Tampa Sports Authority to pay debt service on the bonds and build up a capital improvement fund, and the residual is shared between the county and the incorporated municipalities.

The amount of local option sales tax for repayment of the bonds is dictated in the interlocal agreement and will closely mirror the actual debt service schedule of the bonds. However, the amount of available sales tax receipts from which these amounts are drawn is substantial. The new half-cent sales tax has been levied since December 1, 1996 and a partial year collection estimate of $45.4 million is anticipated for fiscal 1997. An identical half-cent sales tax for indigent care produced a total of $58.9 million in fiscal 1996, and has increased more than 34% in the last four years. Assuming the fiscal year 1996 collections as a base, the first $14.7 million of this revenue stream would go directly to the school board. The remaining $44.2 million would provide ample coverage of the bonds estimated annual debt service of $9.8 million. The Authority would specify the precise amount in a given year needed to meet debt service and capital improvement requirements, with the residual going to the county and incorporated municipalities. The Authority will maintain a debt service reserve funded at maximum debt service with bond proceeds at $13.4 million.
AUTHORITY IS A CONDUIT ISSUER; PLEDGED REVENUES FLOW FROM STATE TO COUNTY

The Tampa Sports Authority is a conduit issuer for the bonds. The Authority was established to develop and maintain sports and recreational facilities in the county. The sales tax is collected by the state and remitted to the county directly, and the county maintains these revenues in a separate Special Revenue Fund. Pursuant to the interlocal agreement the county is required to disburse revenues monthly directly to the Trustee.

There is a weak 1.35 times additional bonds test, but any additional bonds would require approval from the county and cities prior to any changes in the amounts required under the interlocal agreement. Additional bonds are not currently contemplated especially since a guaranteed construction price has been negotiated and a contingency has been established. The bonds have been validated.

Payout is slow. The 30 year term of the bonds is reportedly within the useful life of the facility, and with bonds structure for level annual debt service, over one- half of the principal amount of the bonds is repaid in the last ten years.

The County and the City of Tampa, pursuant to interlocal agreement, are responsible for any operating and maintenance deficiencies related to the operation of the new facility on a two-thirds, one-third basis respectively from non-ad valorem revenues. Pledged local option sales tax funds cannot be used for this purpose.
RECREATIONAL NATURE OF FINANCED FACILITY

The current offering, along with simultaneously-issued Florida State Sales Tax bonds for $29.45 million and Tourist Development Tax bonds for $11.6 million, will be used for the construction of a new 65,000 seat community stadium to be used by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers football team and to construct a practice facility. The stadium, pursuant to a construction agreement, is being built with a guaranteed maximum price of $156 million, and must be substantially complete by September 19, 1998. The facility will be owned and operated by the Tampa Sports Authority. Any delays in project completion would result in lost income from the facility and require the City of Tampa and the county to pay the estimated $3.5 million operating and maintenance expense associated with the current facility being used by the Buccaneers.

Although the facility is for a less than essential government purpose, it is considered an important economic component for the city. The sales tax received majority countywide voter support, proceeds of this separate funding source may be used for infrastructure purposes only. ANALYSTS:
